sections.t: International Silver Stick preview, Nov 26–29 (Whitby, Ontario)
b: The field: 30 teams in six pools of five. 7 of the top 10 in North America and 19 of the top 30 are entered: #1 Pittsburgh Penguins Elite, #2 Vaughan Kings, #3 Bishop Kearney Selects, #5 Toronto Jr Canadiens, #7 Toronto Marlboros, #8 Halton Hurricanes, #10 Hamilton Steel.
Not in the field: #4 Mount St Charles Hockey Academy, #6 Shattuck St Mary's, #9 Chicago Reapers.

Format: Four pool games each from Thursday to Saturday. A win is 2 points and a tie is 1; there is no overtime in pool play. The six pool winners and two wildcards reach the quarterfinals, and the champion is crowned Sunday.
How teams advance: only 8 of the 30 teams reach the quarterfinals. The six pool winners are seeded 1 to 6 and the two best second-place teams get in as wildcards, seeded 7 and 8.

Wildcards and ties: points first, then head-to-head where the teams met, then most wins, then share of goals scored (goals for divided by goals for plus goals against), then fewest goals against. There is no overtime in pool play, so a tie is one point each and every goal counts.
Quarterfinals: the best record plays the worst, and two teams from the same pool cannot meet again until the final.
Pool A: #10 Hamilton Steel (94.13), #13 Chicago Mission (93.86), #32 Mississauga Senators (91.99), #44 Ottawa Valley Titans (91.08), #89 Whitby Wildcats (89.00).
Pool B: #1 Pittsburgh Penguins Elite (96.81), #8 Halton Hurricanes (94.29), #15 Mississauga Rebels (93.35), #20 Central Ontario Wolves (93.08), #38 Kingston Jr Gaels (91.65).
Pool C: #3 Bishop Kearney Selects (95.85), #5 Toronto Jr Canadiens (95.21), #12 Oakland Jr Grizzlies (93.99), #29 Ottawa Jr 67's (92.25), #63 Chatham-Kent Cyclones (90.14).
Pool D: #7 Toronto Marlboros (94.57), #23 North Shore Whitecaps (92.73), #26 Pittsburgh Vengeance (92.35), #31 Elgin Middlesex Canucks (92.03), #78 Thunder Bay Kings (89.30).
Pool E: #2 Vaughan Kings (95.95), #16 York Simcoe Express (93.34), #33 Ottawa Myers Automotive (91.99), #57 Soo Jr Greyhounds (90.39), #70 Windy City Storm (89.59).
Pool F: #11 Little Caesars (94.03), #17 Waterloo Wolves (93.26), #18 Toronto Nationals (93.12), #28 Palmyra Black Knights (92.25), Upper Canada College (not rated).
Hardest pool: Pool B has 4 of the top 20 in North America (#1 Pittsburgh Penguins Elite, #8 Halton Hurricanes, #15 Mississauga Rebels, #20 Central Ontario Wolves) and one automatic spot.
Easiest road: #7 Toronto Marlboros in Pool D. The next-best team in its pool is #23 North Shore Whitecaps.

No favorite: Pool F has no top-10 team but 3 of the top 20 (#11 Little Caesars, #17 Waterloo Wolves, #18 Toronto Nationals). They take points off each other, which makes a wildcard from this pool harder to come by.

Games to circle: #10 Halton Hurricanes against #1 Pittsburgh Penguins Elite, Thu 7:05 PM; #3 Bishop Kearney Selects against #5 Toronto Jr Canadiens, Thu 7:30 PM; #12 Oakland Jr Grizzlies against #5 Toronto Jr Canadiens, Fri 3:40 PM; #15 Mississauga Rebels against #1 Pittsburgh Penguins Elite, Fri 4:25 PM; #12 Oakland Jr Grizzlies against #3 Bishop Kearney Selects, Sat 12:35 PM.
First game: Thursday at 2:15 PM Central. Scores and the pool tables will be here all weekend.
The top scorers coming to Whitby in each pool, by points a game this season (eight or more games on record).

Pool A: Hudson Bryan, Hamilton Steel (#9, 94.41): 21 goals and 25 assists in 23 games; Brett Rossetto, Hamilton Steel (#9, 94.41): 22 goals and 20 assists in 23 games; Mason Marek, Chicago Mission (#13, 94.01): 8 goals and 17 assists in 17 games.

Pool B: Beckham Hunter, Halton Hurricanes (#8, 94.61): 48 goals and 30 assists in 27 games; Isaac Cartier, Halton Hurricanes (#8, 94.61): 24 goals and 36 assists in 27 games; Cameron Cline, Pittsburgh Penguins Elite (#1, 96.81): 25 goals and 23 assists in 25 games.

Pool C: Shihan Wang, Toronto Jr Canadiens (#5, 95.41): 19 goals and 24 assists in 22 games; Smith Vantine, Bishop Kearney Selects (#3, 96.00): 15 goals and 29 assists in 26 games; Kade O'Rourke, Toronto Jr Canadiens (#5, 95.41): 19 goals and 18 assists in 22 games.

Pool D: Nicholas Nacevic, North Shore Whitecaps (#22, 92.95): 23 goals and 25 assists in 25 games; Jayden Challenger, Toronto Marlboros (#7, 94.81): 20 goals and 26 assists in 24 games; Jake Mancino, Toronto Marlboros (#7, 94.81): 17 goals and 29 assists in 25 games.

Pool E: Preston Hebert, Vaughan Kings (#2, 96.10): 18 goals and 25 assists in 26 games; Niko Fegaras, Vaughan Kings (#2, 96.10): 21 goals and 18 assists in 26 games; Joshua Muise, Ottawa Myers Automotive (#32, 92.16): 8 goals and 22 assists in 23 games.

Pool F: Drystan Thomas, Little Caesars (#11, 94.30): 21 goals and 32 assists in 27 games; Keaton Niereisel, Waterloo Wolves (#17, 93.43): 20 goals and 18 assists in 21 games; Liam Weiss, Waterloo Wolves (#17, 93.43): 17 goals and 21 assists in 23 games.
Open any team's page for its pool, its four games and its own players to watch.
Bishop Kearney (#3, 96.00) had the best weekend in the age group: 3-0 in Pittsburgh, including a 4-2 win over Pittsburgh Penguins Elite (#1, 96.81). It leads the Northeast Pack with 25 points.
Mount St Charles (#4, 95.77) has won eight straight league games and sits two points back.
Chicago Mission (#13, 94.01) went 1-2: a 5-4 loss to Mount St Charles, a 3-2 win over Mid-Fairfield with three power-play goals, and a 7-3 loss to Penguins Elite.
In Toronto, Vaughan Kings (#2, 96.10) shut out Toronto Jr Canadiens (#5, 95.41) 2-0 and are still unbeaten at 26-0-1.
Toronto Jr Canadiens (#5, 95.41) answered Sunday with a 3-1 win over Toronto Marlboros (#7, 94.81).
Oakland Jr Grizzlies (#12, 94.17) held off Fox Motors 5-4.
